messages:
maya: Hey — hitting intermittent TLS errors from our Rust SDK when running in the corp-container. Works locally, fails in CI behind our proxy. Error: "error trying to connect: certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate"

maya: Stack log: `reqwest::Error { kind: Request, source: Some( tls: Error { code: 20, kind: InvalidInput, msg: "certificate verify failed" } ) }`

maya: Repro steps: container has /etc/ssl/certs/corp-ca.pem mounted, running curl inside the container succeeds with `--cacert`, but SDK requests fail. Anyone seen this?

sam: Quick check — which TLS backend is the Rust SDK using in your build? rustls or native-tls?

maya: Using the default features from the crate (didn't opt into rustls).

jon: If curl works with `--cacert` then the OS store isn't picked up by the runtime. Try setting SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/corp-ca.pem in the container env and re-run. For reqwest/native-tls that often fixes it.

liz: Also confirm that the CA file is in PEM bundle format (multiple certs concatenated). Single cert vs bundle trips clients.

maya: Good point — it's a bundle. I verified with `openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -in /etc/ssl/certs/corp-ca.pem` — shows multiple entries.

sam: Another angle: our Rust SDK builds with `reqwest` which defers to the platform TLS. If you're on Debian-based container make sure `ca-certificates` is installed. If not, reqwest/native-tls won't find trust anchors.

maya: ca-certificates is installed. Still seeing failures intermittently (some requests succeed).

jon: Intermittent = could be proxy doing MITM with different cert chains on different hosts, or SNI mismatch. Run this to inspect the cert the proxy presents: \n```\nopenssl s_client -showcerts -connect <proxy-host>:<proxy-port> -servername api.redwood.com -CAfile /etc/ssl/certs/corp-ca.pem\n```\nCheck the cert chain and subjectAltName.

maya: Running s_client now... shows proxy returning a cert signed by corp-issuer, CN matches proxy, then it forwards to target. So proxy is MITMing and re-signing.

sam: In that case ensure your CA bundle includes that issuer. Also confirm the SDK isn't doing hostname pinning somewhere. We don't pin hostnames in the SDK.

liz: For streaming connections, note that persistent connections (keep-alive) may reuse a different channel that the proxy intercepts differently. If you have retry logic that reopens sockets, that could explain intermittent behaviour. Try disabling keep-alive as a test.

maya: Good tip — is there an easy env toggle for keep-alive in reqwest?

jon: You can build a Client with `Client::builder().pool_max_idle_per_host(0)` to effectively disable keep-alive pooling. In the SDK we expose a config struct where you can pass a custom reqwest::Client — could try that in a quick patch.

maya: I'll try repro with `SSL_CERT_FILE` and disabling pooling.

sam: If that works, @sam to @maya: I can open a tiny README patch documenting the SSL_CERT_FILE and ca-bundle mounting for CI containers and add a snippet showing how to construct a custom reqwest client for keep-alive workarounds. Want me to draft a PR? :+1:

maya: Yes please, that would help a lot.

devex-bot: Created issue RED-2021: "Rust SDK: docs for corp CA bundles and proxy quirks" (assigned to sam).

maya: Also one more Q — we have a couple of services using mutual TLS. If we need mTLS, what's the recommended way to pass client cert/key into SDK?

sam: For mTLS you can create a custom reqwest client with an Identity: `let id = Identity::from_pem(cert_and_key_pem)?; Client::builder().identity(id).build()?` We'll add an example to the README.

liz: And ensure the key is readable only by the process and mounted from a secret store in CI. Add a short note about file permissions in the docs.

maya: Great. I'll try the env + client tweaks and paste results here. Thanks all :eyes:

sam: @jon can you do a quick code review if I open the docs PR? I might add a tiny integration test that runs a curl check in CI container as smoke test.

jon: Yep, ping me in the PR.

maya: Follow-up: setting `SSL_CERT_FILE` fixed 95% of failures; disabling pool helped for the remaining flakiness. Will add logs later and close the loop in the issue. Thanks! :thumbsup:
